question.:question/problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by ${x}^{2}+(y-4)^{2}+(z-4)^{2}=25$ and the vector field $F=3\left(x\right)\,i+3\left(xz\right)\,j+3\left(3z\right)\,k$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3\left(x\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3\left(xz\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3\left(3z\right)) \\  & =3+0+9 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $5$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}12\,\text{d}V \\  & =12{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =12\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =12\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {5}^{3} \\  & =2000 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field $F=⟨3\left(y-z\right),\,3\left(y-2x\right),\,3\left(x+4z\right)⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of the rectangular solid shown above in the first octant. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3\left(y-z\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3\left(y-2x\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3\left(x+4z\right)) \\  & =0+3+12 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the rectangular solid enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}15\,\text{d}V \\  & =15{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =15\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =15\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot 4 \\  & =240.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(yz-2x\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left(3y\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\left(x+z\right)) \\  & =(-4)+6+2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
